correctness.rationale: Exact killed-chain formula and Cayley-Hamilton recurrence are checked against exhaustive rational paths. The characteristic-polynomial square identity proves the unique rate optimum; Perron eigenvector bounds control all finite-horizon global minima uniformly; local analytic eigen-decomposition proves eventual strict convexity, the 4/(15n) optimizer shift and 9/8 survival prefactor. All quantifiers, endpoints and the limitations on finite-horizon uniqueness are explicit. Standalone verify.py passes 288 checks; infinite claims rest on proof, not tests.

value.rationale: At fixed wet-day frequency, the probability of encountering a paired wet spell is neither monotonically increasing nor decreasing with lag-one persistence over a finite monitoring window. The mathematically natural optimization identifies exact four-day and large-window thresholds and an explicit 1/n finite-window correction, yielding a precise calibration benchmark for rainfall-occurrence models. The restricted natural wet-pair event is the genuine object of interest, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a claimed flood forecast.
